stem:
An analogue signal is to be transmitted to a receiver. Before transmission, the signal passes through an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC). After transmission it passes through a digital-to-analogue converter (DAC) before finally reaching the receiver, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State two advantages of converting the signal into digital form for transmission.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The variation with time of the potential difference (p.d.) of the input signal is shown in Fig. 5.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The ADC has a sampling frequency of 250 Hz and uses 4-bit sampling, with the least significant bit corresponding to 1 mV. The signal is first sampled at time 0, when the sampled bits are 001.
parts.text: State the sampled bits at time 4 ms and time 8 ms.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Part of the signal received by the receiver, after the sampled signal has passed through the DAC, is shown in Fig. 5.3.

[[fig:f3]]

On Fig. 5.3, complete the line to show the received signal for time 0 to time 12 ms.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The ADC in (b) is replaced by one that has a sampling frequency of 500 Hz and uses 3-bit sampling, with the least significant bit corresponding to 2 mV.

On Fig. 5.4, sketch the signal that is now received, after passing through the DAC, from time 0 to time 12 ms.

[[fig:f4]]

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A signal path runs from an input signal through an ADC, along a transmission line, through a DAC, and to a receiver.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A graph of input potential difference in mV against time in ms, with a smooth curve rising to a peak near 6 ms, falling to a trough near 8 ms, and rising again before falling toward 12 ms.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.3
figures.alt: A graph of potential difference in mV against time in ms with a stepped signal at about 1 mV until 4 ms and about 5 mV from 4 ms to 6 ms.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.4
figures.alt: An empty graph grid of potential difference in mV against time in ms, from 0 to 12 ms.
